uncited: The method builds on [Radiance-field optimization](44-radiance-field-optimization.md) by introducing a physically-based rendering formulation within the neural volume.
*   **Degenerate Input:** If the object is not present in an image (mask is all zeros), the loss contribution is zero, but the illumination vector for that image is still optimized.
Uses a hierarchical grid structure to accelerate the query of the neural volume, reducing memory and computation time compared to a single dense MLP [1414-hierarchical-grid-optimization.md].
Represents the scene as a set of 3D Gaussians instead of a neural volume, offering faster rendering but potentially less accurate material decomposition [1795-3d-gaussian-splatting.md].
The foundational method that Neural 3D Volume Decomposition extends.
NeRF optimizes for view-dependent color, while this method optimizes for physical material properties [4972-neural-radiance-fields.md].
*   **Time Complexity:** The rendering time is dominated by the MLP queries for each sample point along each ray.
With $N$ samples per ray and $R$ rays, the complexity is $O(R \cdot N)$.
*   **Memory Complexity:** The memory usage is dominated by the MLP weights and the learnable illumination vectors.
The MLP size is typically small (a few hundred thousand parameters), and the illumination vectors are $q \times 128$.
Optimization is complex and may require pre-trained networks for stability.
*   **When to use:** When the goal is to recover physical material properties and illumination from a set of images, rather than just novel view synthesis.
*   **When not to use:** When only novel view synthesis is needed, or when the input images do not have varying illumination.
